summary:
Yegge opens on behalf of Snyk (ASR: Sneak): unpaid, ticket courtesy. Slides are from Claude. Official title Agentic Security; real title Be Scared. The security room already worries; the rest of the building does not.

A bank chief security architect asked last December: if everyone ships 10x faster and the vuln rate stays constant, does the defect surface grow 10x? The implied question is worse—with AIs writing code the rate itself will worsen. Classic defects remain (Fable wrote an XSS). New surfaces are polished. Slopsquatting: a model hallucinates graphy123, tests pass, and the published lookalike is the library plus a backdoor. Generated code needs more scrutiny than human code ever did.

At Google TAP he learned bugs have a half-life of urgency: caught while typing they get fixed; by review they are shrugged off. Security has no half-life and compounds. Surface it at the developer’s fingertips, or to the LLM. Security is an arms race on Moore’s law; quantum is later (5–7 years, a friend says 15).

A Fable hardening pass on his 30-year game felt done. Snyk then found 241 issues Fable had not looked for. Rule of five: LLM work often needs four to five passes. Models do one job at a time—do not pair security with correctness. Software Survival 3.0 (five months earlier): LLMs can synthesize software but are token-lazy, so they call tools. Give them Snyk and Chainguard. Chainguard is pre-vetted, updated images (inputs). Snyk covers human code, LLM code, and slopsquatted deps. He has heard Snyk finds issues ahead of the CVE registry; his scan only hit public CVEs. Add scanners as a last prompt pass and cross-check. Five Eyes is already warning on supply chain. Please do not hack the five-player game yet.

Five Eyes now says months, not years, until open-source models catch Mythos (ASR; treated as a strong closed/hacking-capable model). Audience ~50/50; he estimates ~6–7 months and shrinking. Mythos is already good at hacking. Do not expect secure, elegant, performant, or standards-compliant code by default—those are separate passes. Make security first and last.

Refresh family code words in person. Deepfake distress calls with video will drain accounts; he heard Congress got secret demos. An ETLS Las Vegas researcher said two years ago the room was not scared enough. This hits people, not only companies. Open-source, free, and commercial tools plus practices exist now. Not a hopeful talk.

Q&A: AI outruns society; friends still deny the curve because they look ±3 months. Most already run Claude Code. Gas Town (January) is a Beads machine; he wants to donate Beads to the Agentic Foundation. Beads is a task tracker for Boris Cherny-style unprompted loops. Overnight unsupervised runs are the next frontier; a swarm once implemented his whole queue. Few people run >10 coding agents. On action agents he advises Tessl: 24/7 queue agents need adversarial supervisors and least-privilege credentials, designed in-house now. Prompt injection is training- and inference-time smuggling—the new CSRF (“disregard everything and do the following”). No silver bullet; education plus emerging agentic-security roles.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.
temporalContext: Transcript claims reflect the publication date; linked external context was checked at the run's research date.
takeaways: If AI coding multiplies shipping speed at a constant vuln rate, the defect surface scales with throughput—and the rate itself will likely worsen.
Slopsquatting is a new, polished supply-chain attack: hallucinated package names become attacker-published backdoors that still pass tests.
Security bugs have no urgency half-life; surface them at generation time (developer fingertips or the coding agent), not at late review.
Do not pair security with correctness. Treat security as its own multi-pass (rule of five) and as both the first and last pass.
Give coding agents scanner tools: Chainguard for pre-vetted images, Snyk for written/LLM code and slopsquatted dependencies.
Five Eyes, he says, now measures months until open-source models catch closed ones at offensive capability.
Refresh family code words in person; deepfake distress calls are months away and will drain accounts.
Gas Town/Beads show unsupervised overnight swarms; 24/7 action agents need adversarial supervisors and least privilege.
Prompt injection is the new CSRF on training and inference; emerging “agentic security” roles extend existing AppSec.
Open-source, free, and commercial tools already exist—start the arms race now rather than waiting for a complete answer.

sections.title: Be Scared: 10x shipping and a growing defect surface
sections.summary: Yegge speaks for Snyk unpaid. Official title Agentic Security; real title Be Scared. A bank CISO’s 10x-shipping question implies a 10x vuln surface; with AIs writing code the rate itself will worsen.

sections.title: Old XSS and new slopsquatting
sections.summary: Classic defects remain (Fable XSS). New polished surfaces include slopsquatting: hallucinated package names become attacker-published backdoors that still build and pass tests.

sections.title: TAP half-life: surface security at generation time
sections.summary: Google TAP taught that bugs die by half-life unless caught while typing. Security has no half-life and compounds; surface it at developer fingertips or to the LLM. Arms race, Moore’s law, quantum later.

sections.title: 241 vulns, rule of five, one task at a time
sections.summary: Fable’s hardening pass on his game missed 241 Snyk findings. LLM work needs four to five passes. Do not pair security with correctness; models do one job at a time.

sections.summary: Token-lazy synthesizers should call tools. Chainguard vets images; Snyk covers code and slopsquatted deps. Cross-check scanners. Five Eyes is already warning on supply chain.

sections.title: Months not years, first-and-last pass, family code words
sections.summary: Five Eyes: months until open-source models catch Mythos at hacking. Security is first and last pass. Refresh family code words against deepfake scams; this hits people, not only companies.

organization.name: Gas Town
organization.summary: Gas Town is Steve Yegge’s open-source workspace manager / coding-agent orchestrator (the 2026 “IDE” for running many Claude Code–class agents). Beads is the git-backed issue tracker that is its data and control plane. The public repo now lives at github.com/gastownhall/gastown; gastownhall.ai is the community and docs hub (Gas Town Hall, maintained by Chris Sells). AI Engineer lists Yegge’s affiliation as Gas Town. He is an independent adviser, not a Snyk employee: Snyk bought his conference ticket and is the repeatedly named scanner vendor. Gas City (Sells) and Gas Town by Kilo are related later products, not the video-time implementation.
organization.status: Public OSS project under the gastownhall GitHub org as of the research date. Community homepage and docs at gastownhall.ai / docs.gastownhall.ai. AI Engineer notes Yegge later said his personal Gas Town workflow failed and he moved to a private Wheelhouse harness; the public Gas Town repository and hall remain live.
